_meta.indication: NGENLA is a human growth hormone analog indicated for treatment of pediatric patients aged 3 years and older who have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, active-controlled, open-label, 52-week noninferiority study comparing somatrogon 0.66 mg/kg/wk versus Genotropin (somatropin) 0.034 mg/kg/day.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive, prepubertal pediatric subjects aged 3 years and older with short stature/growth failure due to growth hormone deficiency (GHD).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized height velocity (AHV) in cm/year after 12 months of treatment; non-inferiority established if lower limit of two-sided 95% CI for the mean difference was ≥ -1.8 cm/year.
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint: mean AHV at week 52 of 10.07 cm/year (somatrogon) vs 9.73 cm/year (Genotropin); treatment difference 0.34 cm/year (95% CI -0.23, 0.91). Lower limit -0.23 exceeded the -1.8 cm/year non-inferiority margin, demonstrating non-inferiority; superiority was not claimed.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) with NGENLA included injection site reactions (42.2% vs 25.2% somatropin), nasopharyngitis (33% vs 28.7%), headache (16.5% vs 21.7%), and pyrexia (16.5% vs 14.8%). Injection site pain occurred more often with somatrogon (39%) than daily somatropin (25%).
target_moa: Somatrogon is a long-acting recombinant hGH derivative whose active moiety has the same primary amino acid sequence as endogenous growth hormone; it binds and activates the GH receptor, stimulating IGF-1 production and epiphyseal growth, replacing deficient native GH.
modality: other (recombinant human growth hormone fusion protein / analog)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held, as this was not the first drug in class and there were no controversial issues warranting external input.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency (GHD); designation made September 29, 2010.

citations.quote: On September 29, 2010, FDA designated MOD-4023 as an orphan drug product for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency (GHD).

summary.text: Standard-review BLA under section 351(a) with Orphan Drug Designation for GHD. The original 2020 application received a Complete Response Letter (January 21, 2022) over immunogenicity and product quality; approval followed a November 22, 2022 resubmission and was granted June 27, 2023. Effectiveness was based on a single adequate and well-controlled phase 3 study (CP-4-006) plus confirmatory mechanistic evidence, acceptable because pediatric GHD is a rare disease.

citations.quote:
Application Type	BLA
Application Number(s)	761184
Priority or Standard	Standard

On November 30, 2020, Pfizer submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) for somatrogon (also known as MOD-4023), a long-acting human growth hormone (hGH) derivative, under Section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act with the following proposed indication: Treatment of pediatric subjects who have growth failure due to growth hormone deficiency.
Somatrogon has been granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) by the Office of Orphan Drug Products for the treatment of GHD.
A single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence is acceptable for this BLA because pediatric GHD is a rare disease.
We acknowledge receipt of your resubmission dated November 22, 2022, which constituted a complete response to our January 21, 2022, action letter.

basis.text: High and persistent incidence of anti-drug antibodies (with some neutralizing antibodies) to somatrogon and its potential implications for loss of efficacy, plus Clinical/Immunology and Product Quality deficiencies.
